A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same task-tree/GIT research. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GIT experiments across five graph domains, including benchmark results, ablations and efficiency comparisons in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds a synthetic large-graph efficiency experiment in Appendix I.

M1.justification: Task-tree construction, mean aggregation, the GraphSAGE backbone, reconstruction with KL regularization, and instruction-based specialization remain unchanged. The expanded virtual-node explanation and newly numbered encoding formula document the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds a synthetic large-graph scenario, ogbn-products x50, constructed from 50 Products replicas connected through 5% edge rewiring. The original real-data coverage and task families remain unchanged; ogbn-papers100M is mentioned only for size comparison.

E2.justification: The standard GNN, self-supervised, OFA, domain-expert and few-shot comparator sets are retained. The Arxiv few-shot comparison moves from v1 Table 16 to v2 Table 26. GIT-SubG already appeared in v1.

E3.justification: The new synthetic-scale experiment fixes batch size at 512 and measures sampling, extraction and encoding times separately. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training settings and few-shot evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I extends the efficiency analysis to test whether task-trees retain their advantage over subgraphs at much larger graph scale, with a computational cost breakdown. Existing regularizer, specialization, training-strategy, model-size and cross-domain analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify at least five runs with different seeds and retain the same standard-deviation reporting practices. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 24 reports total epoch times of 7,211 seconds for GIT-SubG and 2,975 seconds for GIT-Task-Tree, with component costs. These are additional results under the new synthetic-scale conditions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1, 3.3 and 3.5, and Appendix D proofs are substantively unchanged. Numbering the existing mean-encoding formula and reordering terms in the generalization bound do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly centers the contribution on task alignment and newly claims the first theoretical framework addressing task heterogeneity in graph learning. The underlying claims about task-tree transferability, GIT's capabilities and domain specialization remain.

C2.justification: v2 Section 5.2 replaces v1's warning about reduced general inference after specialization with a claim that other-domain performance does not significantly degrade. Yet Appendix J/Table 25 retains the losses and specialization-tax discussion. v1 Appendix F.1's explanation of zero-shot advantages on SFT datasets is also omitted.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly documents synthetic-graph construction, graph sizes, the fixed batch size and runtime components. Existing implementation details, hyperparameter tables, feature alignment and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds an explicit three-part distinction from the already-cited GFT, while Section 2.3 expands positioning against subgraph-based task alignment. Several references are removed, including Verma and Zhang (2019) and Zhang et al. (2023) on specialization.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are substantially revised. Section 2 now combines preliminaries, construction, encoding and comparison; experiments and appendices are extensively reorganized into dedicated topical sections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, Tables 1 and 24 are added, several overview plots are removed, and many displays are relocated or consolidated. The training-strategy ablation moves from v1 Appendix Table 17 to v2 main-text Table 3.

improvement.justification: v2 makes task-tree encoding and its relationship to subgraph methods and GFT clearer, while Appendix I adds concrete evidence for the efficiency claim at synthetic large-graph scale. These provide a limited net gain in clarity and support. The gain is tempered by the more positive specialization statement in Section 5.2, which is in tension with the unchanged losses and caveat in Appendix J/Table 25.
